name: Naphthylaminopropane
summary: Naphthylaminopropane (NAP; code name PAL-287), also known as naphthylisopropylamine (NIPA), is an experimental drug of the amphetamine and naphthylaminopropane families that was under investigation for the treatment of alcohol and stimulant addiction.

pharmacology.text: Naphthylaminopropane is a serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine releasing agent (SNDRA). Its EC50 values for induction of monoamine release are 3.4 nM for serotonin, 11.1 nM for norepinephrine, and 12.6 nM for dopamine. The drug is also an agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B, and 5-HT2C receptors. Its EC50 values are 466 nM at the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor, 40 nM at the serotonin 5-HT2B receptor, and 2.3 nM at the serotonin 5-HT2C receptor.
